topic.title: Drawing Different Shapes
topic.description: Draws polygons from triangle to decagon, each with a random color. Applies the exterior angle formula (360 / sides) and nested loops.

learningNotes.whatILearned: A polygon with `i` sides needs `360 / i` degrees at each corner — the angle follows from the number of sides.
learningNotes.challenges: The one comment in the file says what the line does, not why the angle is what it is.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Write the rule down: the angles of a shape have to add up to 360, so each one is 360 divided by the number of sides.

files.description: Draws triangle to decagon with random colors.

misconceptions: The exterior angle of a regular polygon is 360 divided by its number of sides — that single fact is the whole file
The shape is regular only because every side is the same length; the angle rule alone does not make a square
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**0 + 30 + 5 = 35%**

**This file cannot be run here.** It needs `tkinter`, and this
machine has no display and no `tkinter` — so the 40 points for *it runs* are
not ones I can give, and they are not given. The other two bands are judged
by reading the code, carefully, line by line.

There is a bigger point here, and it is worth saying plainly: **`tkinter`
does not exist on Termux either.** These files cannot be run on the phone
this whole system is built around. They are not broken — they are stranded.

**What is right, by reading**

The maths is right, and it is the maths that is the point. For a shape with `i` sides, each corner turns by `360 / i` — a triangle turns 120°, a pentagon 72°, a decagon 36° — and drawing `i` sides that way closes the shape exactly. The loop runs from 3 to 10 sides, so the file draws a triangle, a square, a pentagon and on up to a decagon, each in a random colour.

**What is not**

The one comment says *Random color for each shape*, which describes the line it sits on and says nothing about the shape. The angle line — `angle = 360 / i` — is the most interesting line in the file and it has no explanation at all.

There is also no comment on why the inner loop counts to `i`, which is what makes the polygon close.

**The one thing to fix first**

```python
angle = 360 / i  # The corners of a shape add up to 360, so each one is 360/i degrees.
```

One line, and the file explains the geometry it is drawing.
